verdict.rationale: Secureframe's MCP docs show that an agent client gets its own credential: through an OAuth-style sign-in the client "receives its own token", and an API key option covers browserless CI or scripts. That gives each agent a distinct credential rather than a shared user secret, but nothing in the evidence shows the scope or permissions can be restricted to least privilege. Missing for 10: documented per-credential scopes or permission limits, read-only or resource-restricted tokens, credential revocation and rotation controls, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can issue scoped/least-privilege API credentials for an agent

citations.quote: you sign in to Secureframe and approve access, and the client receives its own token. There is nothing to generate, copy, or store yourself, and no secret ends up in a config file.
API key For setups with no browser — CI jobs, scripts, serv
Any MCP-capable client (Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor, and others) can connect, letting you ask an assistant to look things up and take actions on your behalf.
